THE QUESTION

Does 40% more solder
make a better joint?

The result comes from the pinned native Surface Evolver engine. SolderShape adds the KiCad workflow, interpretation and reproducible export. It does not introduce a new solver.

03 / KEEP THE QUESTION REPRODUCIBLE

From a pad
to a testable assumption.

A useful review keeps the input, the result and its limits together. Every assumption edit clears the current result. A saved input is never presented as a fresh computation.

  1. 01

    Choose an actual pad

    Select source copper from the board or a KiCad footprint. Declare the wetting boundary and opposing pad.

  2. 02

    Compare the assumptions

    Prescribe a gap or supported load. Change volume or diameter and inspect each native equilibrium.

  3. 03

    Keep the evidence

    Export exact inputs, readable review, CSV, meshes, raw logs and hashes. Replay the trusted requests.

  4. 04

    Plan the measurement

    Use the study and lab materials to specify what must be measured before a physical decision.

04 / KNOW WHAT THE EVIDENCE SAYS

Numerical agreement.
Physical questions still open.

The model assumes an isolated equilibrium joint between fully wetted, pinned circular rims. Wetting chemistry, thermal reflow, substrate obstacles and neighboring-joint effects remain outside it.

ESTABLISHED FOR THE RECORDED CASE

You can inspect and replay it.

The archive retains both native computations, the original board, selected-pad mapping, input identity, meshes, logs and a SHA-256 manifest. Local replay reproduced both forces with zero difference on the recorded engine.

PHYSICAL QUALIFICATION REMAINS OPEN

It has not earned production trust.

Published-data force validation has unresolved failures. No new solder specimens were measured. The outside-lab force fixture and height coupon are planning material, not validated manufacturing tools.

No package motion, bridging, yield, fatigue or reliability prediction follows from this comparison.
